mainTopic: Whether meat slaughtered on שבת or יום הכיפורים may be eaten that day, according to רבי יהודה's rule of הכנה, and whether רבי יהודה accepts ברירה.
overview: The משנה says that someone who slaughters on שבת or יום הכיפורים has done a serious sin, but the שחיטה itself is kosher. רב adds that the meat may not be eaten that same day, and the scholars said this follows רבי יהודה. רבי אבא explains that this is רבי יהודה's rule of הכנה: something that was not ready before שבת may not be used on שבת, like an animal that died on שבת and only then became food for dogs. אביי objects that the slaughtered animal was always meant for people. רבי אבא answers that a living animal is kept for raising, not eating. אביי then asks how anyone may slaughter on יום טוב according to רבי יהודה. רבי אבא answers that a living animal stands for both purposes, and slaughtering it shows after the fact that it was meant for eating. That answer relies on ברירה, and the גמרא challenges it, because רבי יהודה is known to reject ברירה. It begins checking the source for that claim with a ברייתא about wine bought from כותים, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Slaughtering on שבת or יום הכיפורים is still valid
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that שחיטה done on שבת or יום הכיפורים is kosher, even though the person who did it is liable to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone slaughters an animal on שבת or on יום הכיפורים, even though he deserves death for doing it, his slaughter is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a basic rule: breaking שבת by slaughtering does not make the שחיטה itself invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate things are in play here. One is the sin of doing מלאכה on a holy day, which is very serious. The other is whether the animal was slaughtered correctly. The משנה says the sin does not ruin the kosher status of the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the text the גמרא will discuss
Kosher slaughter of an animal
Liable with his life, meaning he deserves the death penalty
Valid, kosher

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who slaughters on Shabbat or on Yom Kippur,
even though he is liable with his life,
phrases.notes: Slaughtering is one of the forbidden kinds of work. Doing it on purpose on שבת carries the death penalty, and on יום הכיפורים it carries כרת.

phrases.english: his slaughter is valid.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחיטה done on שבת or יום הכיפורים is valid, even though the person who did it is liable to death.

steps.title: רב: The meat is forbidden to eat that day
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that even though the שחיטה is kosher, the meat may not be eaten on that day. The scholars said this follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב הונא said that חייא בר רב taught in the name of רב: The meat is forbidden to eat for that day. The scholars of the study hall tended to say that this follows the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a limit to the משנה: the animal is kosher, but nobody may eat it on that same day. The scholars connect this ruling to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the שחיטה is valid. רב says that does not mean the meat is ready to eat right away, because there is a ban on eating it for that day only. The scholars then tie this ban to a known opinion of רבי יהודה, without yet saying which one.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden to eat
For the day, meaning only for that same day
The group of scholars in the study hall
They tended to say, they took the view

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב is arguing with the משנה. The משנה says the שחיטה is kosher, and רב agrees. He only adds that eating the meat is not allowed on that day.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna said,

phrases.english: Ḥiyya bar Rav taught in the name of Rav:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, דָּרַשׁ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the משנה's ruling: the שחיטה is valid, but eating is forbidden that day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat slaughtered on שבת or יום הכיפורים is forbidden to eat on that day. The scholars say this follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Which teaching of רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which specific opinion of רבי יהודה the scholars meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which ruling of רבי יהודה is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next move: we need to know which of רבי יהודה's rulings is the source for רב's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה has many rulings, so just saying 'it follows רבי יהודה' is not clear. The גמרא wants the exact source so we understand why the meat is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one?

phrases.english: Which Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: He means: which ruling of רבי יהודה are they talking about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarity on the scholars' claim in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific ruling of רבי יהודה is the basis for forbidding the meat that day.

steps.title: רבי אבא: It is רבי יהודה's rule about preparation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says it is רבי יהודה's rule of הכנה. רבי יהודה forbids cutting up an animal that died on שבת for dogs, because it was not ready before שבת. In the same way, an animal slaughtered on שבת was not ready to eat before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: It is רבי יהודה's ruling about preparation, as we learned in a משנה: One may cut up gourds in front of an animal, and a נבלה in front of dogs. רבי יהודה says: If it was not already a נבלה before שבת, it is forbidden, because it is not something that was prepared. We see that since it was not prepared from yesterday, it is forbidden. Here too, since the meat was not prepared from yesterday, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers the question by pointing to a משנה where רבי יהודה forbids using on שבת something that was not ready before שבת. He then applies that same rule to our animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, an animal that dies on שבת turns into a נבלה that day. רבי יהודה says it may not be given to dogs, because before שבת it was not 'ready' as dog food. רבי אבא compares this to our case: before שבת the animal was alive and its meat was not ready to eat, so meat that became ready only on שבת is forbidden that day.

keyTerms.meaning: Preparation: something must be ready for use before שבת or יום טוב begins
Prepared, ready for use
Gourds
An animal that died without kosher slaughter
From yesterday, meaning from before the holy day
So we see, apparently

steps.whyThisMatters: This links the rule about eating meat slaughtered on שבת to the larger topic of מוקצה and things that were not ready before שבת.

phrases.english: So we see: since it was not prepared from yesterday, it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Here too, since it was not prepared from yesterday, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה דַּהֲכָנָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 by naming רבי יהודה's rule of הכנה and applying it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is רבי יהודה's rule of הכנה: something not ready before שבת is forbidden on שבת, and the slaughtered meat was not ready before שבת.

steps.title: אביי: The cases are not alike
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the comparison fails. The נבלה changed from people-use to dog-use on שבת, but the slaughtered animal was meant for people before and is still meant for people now.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are these cases really alike? There, at first the animal was ready for people, and now it is ready for dogs. Here, at first the animal was ready for people, and now it is still ready for people!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבי אבא's comparison by showing a key difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's case, the animal's use really changed on שבת, from people to dogs, so it is a new thing that was not ready. In our case, אביי says the animal was always meant for people, before and after the שחיטה, so nothing new happened on שבת and there should be no problem of הכנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really similar? A way of attacking a comparison
At first, originally
Now
There (the other case) / here (our case)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Are they comparable?
There, at first it was prepared for a person,
and now it is prepared for dogs.
Here, at first it was prepared for a person,
and now it is prepared for a person!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison רבי אבא made in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's comparison between the נבלה case and the animal slaughtered on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נבלה changed its use on שבת (people to dogs), but the slaughtered animal stayed meant for people, so no new 'unprepared' item came into being.

steps.title: A living animal is kept for raising, not for eating
steps.stepSummary: The response to אביי: a living animal is not thought of as food. It is kept for raising, so the meat really became something new on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think a living animal is set aside for eating? A living animal is set aside for raising!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers אביי's challenge by rejecting his starting point, that a living animal was 'ready for people' to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed the animal was always meant as food. The answer is that while it is alive, an animal is normally kept for breeding and raising, not eating. So its becoming food on שבת is a real change, just like the נבלה, and רבי יהודה's rule of הכנה does apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really think? Used to reject someone's assumption
While it is alive
Stands for, is set aside for
For raising, for breeding

steps.whatToRemember: רב forbids eating meat slaughtered on שבת for that day, based on רבי יהודה's rule of הכנה. A living animal counts as kept for raising, not as food, so meat that became food on שבת was not 'prepared' before שבת.

phrases.english: Do you think that an animal during its lifetime
phrases.notes: This answers אביי and defends רבי אבא's comparison.

phrases.english: is designated for eating?
An animal during its lifetime is designated for raising!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ לַאֲכִילָה עוֹמֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by denying that the living animal was ever 'prepared for people'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי assumed a living animal is already meant as food, so nothing changed when it was slaughtered on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: A living animal is kept for raising, so becoming food on שבת is a real change, and the rule of הכנה applies just as with the נבלה.

steps.title: Then how can anyone slaughter on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: If a living animal is not considered food, slaughtering it on יום טוב should create something 'new', so it should be forbidden according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, according to רבי יהודה, how are we allowed to slaughter an animal on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבי אבא's answer from Step 6. If a living animal is not food, how is slaughtering on יום טוב ever allowed according to רבי יהודה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said a living animal is set aside for raising, not eating, so its meat is 'new' on the day it is slaughtered. On יום טוב cooking and slaughtering are allowed, but only for food that was ready before the day began. If the animal was never 'food' before יום טוב, רבי יהודה's rule of הכנה should forbid it, and that cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if what you just said is true, then a problem follows
A festival day, when preparing food is allowed
How do we slaughter?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about whether slaughtering on יום טוב is allowed. Everyone agrees it is. The question is how Step 6's logic can fit with that accepted practice.

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if a living animal is really kept for raising and is not food, as Step 6 said.

phrases.english: an animal, according to רבי יהודה,
on a יום טוב, how do we slaughter it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בְּהֵמָה לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב הֵיכִי שָׁחֲטִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 6 by drawing out an unacceptable result.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 6 that a living animal is not considered food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a live animal is not food, slaughtering it on יום טוב creates new food on the day itself, which רבי יהודה's הכנה rule should forbid. Yet slaughtering on יום טוב is clearly allowed.

steps.title: The animal stands for both, and the slaughtering shows which
steps.stepSummary: A living animal stands both for eating and for raising. Once it is slaughtered, it becomes clear after the fact that it was always meant for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A living animal stands for eating and also stands for raising. If it was slaughtered, it becomes clear that it stood for eating. If it was not slaughtered, it becomes clear that it stood for raising.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: a living animal is undecided, kept for either eating or raising. Slaughtering it shows after the fact that it was food all along.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adjusts Step 6. The animal is not simply 'not food'; its purpose is open. The final act decides backward what it was from the start. So on יום טוב the meat counts as having been food before the day began, and there is no problem of הכנה. This idea of deciding backward is called ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands (is set aside) for eating
Stands for raising or breeding
It became clear (after the fact)

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer depends on ברירה, which opens the next challenge: does רבי יהודה accept ברירה at all?

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This continues the back-and-forth from Steps 4–7: רבי אבא answering אביי.

phrases.english: It stands for eating, and it stands for raising.
If it was slaughtered, it became clear that it stood for eating;
if it was not slaughtered, it became clear that it stood for raising.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: עוֹמֶדֶת לַאֲכִילָה וְעוֹמֶדֶת לְגַדֵּל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refines the earlier claim: the animal's status is open and is settled after the fact.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A living animal is simply not food, so all slaughtering on יום טוב creates new food.
steps.terutzMaskana: A living animal is meant for both purposes. Slaughtering shows backward that it was food all along, so slaughtering on יום טוב does not break רבי יהודה's rule of הכנה.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה does not accept ברירה
steps.stepSummary: The answer in Step 8 relies on ברירה, yet רבי יהודה is known to reject ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יהודה does not hold of ברירה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks Step 8. Its answer works only with ברירה, and רבי יהודה does not accept that principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the slaughtering 'reveals backward' what the animal was for. That is exactly ברירה. If רבי יהודה rejects ברירה, the answer cannot explain his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Clarification after the fact: a later act shows what was true from the start
He does not hold (of this idea)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵירָה!
phrases.english: But רבי יהודה does not hold of ברירה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵירָה
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of ברירה in Step 8 to explain רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An answer based on ברירה cannot explain the view of a sage who rejects ברירה.

steps.title: Where do we know that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the claim that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה, and starts to suggest one.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? If we say it is from what was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check the source of the claim in Step 9. This is a setup line that leads into the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before using 'רבי יהודה rejects ברירה' as a challenge, the גמרא wants its proof. The words אי נימא (if we say) hint that the first suggested source may not hold up in the end.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
If we say: brings a suggestion that may later be rejected

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
If we say it is from what was taught in a ברייתא:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the claim in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה.

steps.title: The case of wine bought from כותים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a buyer of untithed wine wants to name the תרומה and tithes now, take them out later, and drink right away. רבי מאיר allows it; רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who buys wine from the כותים says: 'Two לוגין that I will separate later are hereby תרומה, ten are מעשר ראשון, nine are מעשר שני.' He redeems the מעשר שני and drinks right away. This is the view of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the suggested source: a ברייתא where רבי יהודה forbids drinking wine whose תרומה and tithes will only be picked out later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allows it because the later separation shows backward which wine was the תרומה and tithes, which is ברירה. רבי יהודה forbids it, which seems to show he rejects ברירה. This is the proof proposed for the claim in Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Samaritans, who were not trusted to separate תרומה and tithes
The portion given to a כהן
First tithe, given to a לוי
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money

They forbid

steps.confusionAlert: The wine is not being separated now. He only names amounts now and plans to pick out the actual wine later. That is why this case is about ברירה.
